mono-20111.d: An old refracting telescope stands on its tall tripod, tilted at the sky with its finder scope ready. It has been pointed upwards for so long it has forgotten what the ground looks like.
mono-20111.t: One antique refracting telescope with a finder scope, eyepiece and dew cap, on an altazimuth head and a three-legged tripod, standing on a ruled floor with its shadow

mono-20127.d: A Ferris wheel stands face on, its spokes running in to one hub and its cabins hung round the rim. It goes nowhere at great expense and everyone queues for it anyway.
mono-20127.t: A single Ferris wheel seen face on, its spokes, rim and hanging cabins on an A-frame over a small station and a ground line

mono-20130.d: A stone observatory rises in three ringed storeys to a ribbed dome with its observing slit opened to the sky. The building does its best work at night and keeps its curtains open on purpose.
mono-20130.t: A domed observatory on a round, three-storey stone drum, the shutter slit of the dome open along one rib, steps at its foot

mono-20131.d: A baroque church front fills the end of a narrow street, its domed towers rising over a rose window and an arched door. The houses either side have been leaning in for a better look for a few hundred years.
mono-20131.t: A baroque church front with two onion-domed towers and a third domed tower, a rose window over the arched door, old houses lining the street on either side and a paved square in front

mono-20150.d: Above the ground, an old oak stands bare for the winter; below it, a vixen and her cubs sleep in an earth among its roots. The tree, presumably, has not been told.
mono-20150.t: An old English oak in winter cut away below ground: the bare crown above, the roots spreading through the soil below, and a fox earth among the roots with a vixen and her cubs asleep, a tunnel rising to the surface

mono-20151.d: Dürer never saw a rhinoceros. He cut this one in 1515 from a letter and a rough sketch, armour plates and all, and for more than two centuries it was what Europe believed a rhinoceros looked like.
mono-20151.t: Albrecht Dürer's 1515 woodcut rhinoceros, the armoured beast he cut without ever seeing one, from a letter and a sketch sent from Lisbon: its head, horn, scaled legs and plated shoulder, with his own "1515 RHINOCERVS" and monogram, and the caption "DRAWN FROM A RUMOR." under it

mono-20152.d: In 1665 Robert Hooke put a flea under his microscope and engraved what he saw, armour plates, bristles, claws and all. London had never seen anything like it.
mono-20152.t: Robert Hooke's 1665 engraving of a flea from Micrographia, shown close: the head with its eye, the plated thorax and the two front legs with their claws, Hooke's plate letters kept, with the caption "Nobody had looked this closely before." under it

mono-20153.d: Sixteen pasta shapes, drawn and named the way a naturalist would catalogue beetles. From spaghetti to radiatori, every one is a different answer to holding sauce.
mono-20153.t: Sixteen pasta shapes drawn like the plates of a naturalist's field guide, in a four-by-four chart under the heading "PASTA / A FIELD GUIDE", each shape named below it: spaghetti, penne rigate, farfalle, fusilli, rigatoni, conchiglie, orecchiette, rotelle, cavatappi, tortellini, ravioli, gemelli, radiatori, ditalini, campanelle, lasagne

mono-20154.d: The more horsepower, the worse the decisions, plotted from a bicycle to a dragster that leaves the chart altogether. One minivan sits far below the curve.
mono-20154.t: A scatter chart titled "HORSEPOWER VS. POOR DECISIONS": a bicycle, a scooter, a family hatchback, a motorcycle, a 1960s sports car and a dragster climb a trend curve that runs off the top of the print, while a family minivan sits alone well below it

mono-20155.d: The closing shot of an old film: the sun goes down on the horizon, a small boat sails off, and "the end" sits on the water. Quiet, and final.
mono-20155.t: The words "the end" in large lowercase type, "end" sitting on the horizon of a calm sea at sunset, with a striped half sun setting just after it, the sun's glittering path on the water, a small sailboat heading out and two gulls, drawn in linocut ripple lines

mono-20156.d: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006; nine years later New Horizons flew past it on 14 July 2015 and photographed the heart-shaped plain on its face. The evidence, pasted up like a punk flyer.
mono-20156.t: A punk-zine photocopy collage: ransom-note letters cut from different typefaces spell "PLUTO WAS FRAMED"; below, a coarse halftone print of New Horizons' photograph of Pluto, heart and all, taped down on a torn print, with a cut-out of the New Horizons probe, its dotted flight path and a typed label "NEW HORIZONS / 14 JULY 2015"

mono-20157.d: A sailing boat is becalmed when the wind dies and it can no longer move under sail; the sails hang slack and still water can mirror the hull. Every sailor has sat through it, and most have said this line over the radio.
mono-20157.t: A small sloop becalmed at sunset, side on, its mainsail dumped on the boom and its jib hanging slack; the glassy water mirrors it as the same drawing flipped and broken into horizontal dashes that fade with depth. A striped seventies half sun sits on the horizon, its reflection a column of short broken dashes. Below, in letter-spaced monospaced capitals: MAKING EXCELLENT PROGRESS

mono-20158.d: A wooden boat hauled out for a refit is sanded back to bare wood and painted again, one stretch of hull at a time. Some refits take a season; some outlast the people who started them.
mono-20158.t: A photograph in halftone of a classic wooden gaff cutter hauled out in a boatyard, seen from the side: the front half of her topsides sanded to clean bare planking, the back half still in old dark paint, chipped and peeling; tape along the waterline, a ladder against her, her mast on trestles behind. Above, in letter-spaced condensed capitals: NEARLY FINISHED, and under it, small: SINCE 1987

mono-20159.d: Draw the bar from the fire, raise the hammer, strike, quench. Four frames off one roll, and the whole of a smith's work in each of them. Only what the forge lights is printed; the night of the shop is the shirt.
mono-20159.t: A 35 mm contact strip running down the back, four frames of the same moustached blacksmith at night, lit only by the forge: pulling a glowing bar from the coal fire with tongs; hammer raised over the anvil, the bar held in the tongs; the hammer landing in a fan of sparks; the bar plunged into a wooden water barrel, thin threads of steam rising. Sprocket holes down both edges, frame numbers 1 2 3 4 in the gaps

mono-20160.d: A ketch carries her sail on two masts, the taller forward, so the canvas is split into pieces a small crew can handle. Drawn here the way a sail plan is: every seam, stay and plank.
mono-20160.t: A fine pen-and-ink drawing of a two-masted ketch under full sail on still water, seen from the side, bowsprit to the left: firm spars and hull with thin plank lines, the sails light outlines with their seams in rows of round dots, a waterline, broken water lines and a stippled reflection that fades out downward. Above it, light and letter-spaced: KETCH, under it Maritime · Sail plan, over a rule as long as the hull

mono-20161.d: The breath of the wok: the second the flame jumps the lip and the rice leaves the pan. Only what the fire lights is printed; the rest of the kitchen is the shirt.
mono-20161.t: A carbon-steel wok mid-toss over a roaring burner at night: a sheet of flame rolls over the lip, fried rice, whole prawns and spring-onion rings hang frozen in the air above it, and the cook's hand grips the handle at the lower right, the arm lost in the dark; the burner fades out at the bottom

mono-20162.d: The Nordwand at night, with five rope teams' headlamps on it. The mountain is the real one: every line comes from swisstopo's two-metre survey of the Eiger, cut like an old engraving and lit only by the moon.
mono-20162.t: The Eiger (3,967 m, Bernese Alps) at night, seen from the west-north-west near Kleine Scheidegg: the summit pyramid, the north face on the left in deep shadow, the moonlit west flank on the right running up to the summit, the skyline as a fine line and stars above. On the north face, the headlamps of five rope teams climb towards the summit; the drawing fades out at its foot and sides in an oval vignette

mono-20163.d: The whole road from barley to the bottle, step by step: malt, grist, mash, a hopped boil, the fermenter and the conditioning tank. Each vessel is drawn as a brewer knows it and labelled with what it does.
mono-20163.t: The brewing process as a flow chart of pen drawings under the heading HOW BEER IS MADE: malting, milling and mashing across the top, boiling (with hops added), fermenting and conditioning across the middle, and packaging into bottles, cans and a keg below, each step with its vessel, a heading and one line saying what happens

mono-20164.d: Juniper, coriander, angelica, bitter orange and orris: the five botanicals at the heart of a classic dry gin. Juniper leads, as it must: a gin is a spirit that tastes first of juniper.
mono-20164.t: A plate of the five classic gin botanicals under the heading GIN BOTANICALS, each with its Latin name in italic: a sprig of juniper with berries (Juniperus communis), coriander in flower with its seeds (Coriandrum sativum), angelica root with a cut slice (Angelica archangelica), a curl of bitter orange peel (Citrus × aurantium), and orris, the iris rhizome with slices and a flower (Iris germanica)

mono-20165.d: Terraces of vines climbing a hill to a stone farmhouse and its cypresses, with the harvest hanging heavy in the front row. A landscape drawn the old way, line by line.
mono-20165.t: A terraced hillside vineyard seen through an arched window under the heading VINEYARD: curving rows of vines held by dry-stone walls climb to a stone farmhouse among cypresses and an olive tree, a hill town on the far ridge; in the foreground vines on wooden posts hang with bunches of grapes over a dirt track

mono-20166.d: Malting in four steps: the grain is steeped in water, left to sprout, then dried in a kiln to stop it, and what is left is the malt a brewer mashes. Above it, the barley ear and a grain cut open to its husk, endosperm and germ.
mono-20166.t: A plate of barley and its malting: an ear of barley (Hordeum vulgare); a barley grain whole and in longitudinal section, its husk (lemma), endosperm and germ (embryo) named; and four grains for the stages of malting, each with a line on what happens: 1. steeping, 2. germination, 3. kilning, 4. malt

mono-20167.d: The grapevine as an old botanical plate: a leafy branch with its tendrils and a full bunch, and beside it a pruned cane with the dormant bud next year's fruit will grow from. Line and hatching, the captions under each part.
mono-20167.t: A plate of the grapevine, Vitis vinifera: a branch with three leaves, tendrils and a hanging bunch of grapes, and a pruned cane with its dormant bud, each with a caption in a serif hand

mono-20168.d: A conical fermenter at work: kräusen on top, CO2 rising through the wort, and yeast settling towards the cone's dump valve. Beside it the yeast itself under magnification, budding and giving off the gas.
mono-20168.t: A conical fermenter drawn in cutaway, its parts named: CO2 to the blow-off, a pressure relief valve, kräusen (yeast foam), fermenting wort, rising CO2 bubbles, yeast in suspension, a cooling jacket and the yeast dump valve; beside it budding yeast cells under magnification, the budding cell, the daughter cell and a CO2 bubble named

mono-20169.d: An oak barrel drawn the way a cooper plans one: the elevation, the 24 staves fanned out in an exploded view, the hoops in three pairs and the riveted joint that closes each. Quarter-sawn European oak, galvanised steel, and every part with its size.
mono-20169.t: A cooper's drawing of an oak barrel: its elevation with dimensions (900 mm tall, heads 570 mm across), the stave construction in an exploded view with a stave's sizes (24 staves), the top, middle and bottom hoops, the riveted lap joint and its rivet, and a material key: European oak (Quercus robur / Quercus petraea) staves and heads, galvanised steel hoops, steel rivets

mono-20170.d: How a spirit is made in copper: the wash boils in the pot, its vapour climbs the swan neck and runs down the lyne arm into a worm coiled in cold water, and comes out as spirit. A wood fire underneath and every part named, the way the old distillers drew it.
mono-20170.t: A copper pot still drawn in cutaway over a wood fire in a brick hearth, its parts named: the fermented wash boiling in the pot, the cut-away neck showing the vapour's path, the swan neck, the lyne arm (vapour pipe), the manway, the worm tub (condenser) with its copper worm coiled in cooling water, cold water in and warm water out, the condensate (spirit) dripping into a jug for the distillate

mono-20171.d: A smoothing plane, four chisels from a quarter inch to an inch, a mallet, a pair of spring dividers, a brace and a panel saw, numbered like a page of an old hardware catalogue. The kit of a bench joiner, engraved line by line.
mono-20171.t: A catalogue page of hand tools, each numbered with its size: No. 101 smoothing plane (9 in.), No. 201-204 chisels (1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and 1 in.), No. 301 mallet (head 2 1/2 in.), No. 401 dividers (span 6 in.), No. 501 brace (12 in.) and No. 601 panel saw (22 in.)

mono-20172.d: A classic motorcycle drawn as a workshop sheet: the side view with its dimensions, and the carburettor, the front drum brake, the rear sprocket, the engine and a rear shock in detail. Callouts and a table of specifications in a draughtsman's typewriter lettering.
mono-20172.t: A workshop sheet of a classic motorcycle: its side view with dimensions (1980 mm long, 1330 mm wheelbase, 1000 mm high) and four callouts (side panel, exhaust pipe, engine, seat); details A to E of the carburettor in two views, the front drum brake in section, the rear sprocket, the engine from the right and a rear shock absorber, each with its sizes; and a short table of specifications

mono-20173.d: Five climbers on a snow ridge, roped and climbing, and the range rising peak behind peak beyond them. The long day before the top, drawn line by line.
mono-20173.t: A high mountain range drawn in pen, peak behind peak; in the foreground five climbers roped up on a snow ridge, heading for the top

mono-20174.d: Leaning hard against the kite, bar in both hands, the board throwing spray. The four lines run up to a kite at the top of the sheet: the whole pull of the wind in one drawing.
mono-20174.t: A kitesurfer leaning back against the pull of the kite, the bar in both hands and the harness hooked in, the board cutting spray from the water; the kite high above on its four lines, and the word KITESURFING spaced out beneath

mono-20175.d: A branching stony coral drawn as an old museum plate: the colony, a smaller piece, and one corallite from above and in section, its radiating walls laid open. The animal that builds reefs, one polyp cup at a time.
mono-20175.t: A natural history plate of a branching stony coral under the caption CORAL.: a large branch with its knobbed tips, a smaller colony, and a single corallite seen from above and cut in section

mono-20176.d: Four emperor penguins stand round a downy chick on the ice. The largest penguins alive raise their young through the Antarctic winter.
mono-20176.t: Five emperor penguins standing together on the ice, two tall adults in the middle with a downy chick between them and two more adults at the sides, under the heading ANTARCTICA

mono-20177.d: Thousands of small fish wheeling into a spiral, packed tight at the centre and breaking up into strays at the edges. The shape a shoal makes when something is hunting it.
mono-20177.t: A shoal of small fish turning in a spiral, seen from above: dense in the coils towards the centre and thinning to single fish at the edges

mono-20178.d: The white whale of the Arctic, rising through the water with its rounded melon and its flippers out. Drawn in outline and stipple, its range written underneath.
mono-20178.t: A beluga whale rising through the water, drawn in outline with stipple shading, its flippers and fluke spread; the caption BELUGA and RANGE: ARCTIC OCEAN beneath

mono-20179.d: The humpback inside and out: its body with the long knobbed flippers it is named for, its skeleton, and the baleen it strains its food through. Every part labelled, as on a museum plate.
mono-20179.t: A natural history plate of the humpback whale, Megaptera novaeangliae, under the heading WHALE: the whale whole with its blowhole, dorsal fin, fluke, ventral pleats and long pectoral fin named; its skeleton with skull, mandible, rib cage, vertebral column and the long phalanges of the flipper; and the baleen plates in detail

mono-20180.d: The common octopus, its arms spiralling out in every direction, each lined with suckers. An old natural history engraving, the Latin name set beneath.
mono-20180.t: A common octopus, Octopus vulgaris, seen from above with its eight arms curling outwards and their suckers showing, the caption OCTOPUS and its Latin name beneath

mono-20181.d: Fitz Roy at the centre, Cerro Torre at its side and San Lorenzo, the range's highest, to the left, each peak named with its height. A trekker's panorama of the southern Andes, drawn in line.
mono-20181.t: A pen panorama of the peaks of southern Patagonia, five of them named with their heights: Cerro Fitz Roy 3,405 m, Cerro San Lorenzo 3,706 m, Cerro Torre 3,128 m, Cerro Huemul 2,677 m and Cerro Vespignani 2,146 m, a lake winding between the ranges; the heading PATAGONIA and the coordinates 49.3° S 73.1° W

mono-20182.d: A signpost at El Calafate, the gateway to the glaciers: Ushuaia at the end of the world, El Chaltén for Fitz Roy, Torres del Paine across the border, and Buenos Aires more than two and a half thousand kilometres north. The road distances of a Patagonian trip in one post.
mono-20182.t: A wooden signpost at El Calafate, 0 km, its arms pointing to Buenos Aires 2,727 km, Ushuaia 878 km, Bariloche 1,493 km, Torres del Paine 316 km, Puerto Natales 270 km, El Chaltén 220 km and Río Gallegos 314 km

mono-20183.d: The southernmost city in the world, seen from the Beagle Channel: snow on the peaks, the town along the shore, boats at the quay. Its coordinates written beneath, as on an old view.
mono-20183.t: Ushuaia from the water: snow-capped peaks behind forested hills, the town on the shore with its church spire, sailing boats and a ship at the quay reflected in the Beagle Channel; the caption USHUAIA and the coordinates 54.8019° S 68.3030° W

mono-20184.d: A caye off Belize with a hut under the palms and a jetty over coral heads and clear water. The coordinates beneath fall on Lighthouse Reef, the atoll of the Great Blue Hole.
mono-20184.t: A palm-fringed caye with a wooden hut and a jetty running out over clear water and patches of coral, under the heading BELIZE, the coordinates 17.3167° N 87.5342° W beneath
